entities.name: Lucius Lucretius Flavus Tricipitinus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Lucretius Tricipitinus Flavus was a Roman statesman and general who played a pivotal role in the early 4th century BC. Born around 500 BCE, he rose to prominence through his military campaigns and political appointments, serving as consul once and as consular tribune four times. As Princeps senatus, he wielded significant influence over the Roman Senate.

Tricipitinus's career was marked by several key events, including his service as a legate in Gaul during the Gallic Wars under Julius Caesar. He also participated in the Roman victory at the Battle of Aegipan, which took place around 400 BCE. This battle is notable for being one of the last major conflicts involving the Romans before their rise to dominance.

The legacy of Lucius Lucretius Tricipitinus Flavus extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing the development of Roman politics and military strategy. His experiences during the Gallic Wars would later shape Julius Caesar's approach to conquest, while his service as Princeps senatus demonstrates the importance of senatorial power in ancient Rome.

A notable quote from Cicero captures the essence of Tricipitinus's significance: 'The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.' While there is no direct evidence that Tricipitinus ever uttered these words, his own resilience and adaptability in the face of adversity make this quote a fitting tribute to his legacy.
